description: An empirical study comparing perceived load performance across rendering strategies. Proposes a lightweight metric correlating skeleton-screen timing with user satisfaction scores.
title: Measuring Perceived Performance in Single-Page Applications

description: Presents API design patterns that make accessible output the default in component libraries, evaluated through a case study of three production design systems.
title: Accessible by Default: Component API Patterns for Inclusive Design Systems

description: Introduces the idea of a “contrast budget” for dark interfaces and provides tooling to audit token palettes against WCAG contrast requirements.
title: Dark Mode Done Right: Contrast Budgets for Low-Light Interfaces

description: An audit of the hundred most-visited news sites, quantifying how third-party scripts inflate load times — and a bundling strategy that cut median script cost by a third.
title: The Cost of Convenience: Third-Party Script Bloat on News Sites

description: A pipeline for transforming a single token source into platform-native themes for web, iOS, and Android, with drift detection wired into CI.
title: Tokens in Translation: Keeping Design Systems Consistent Across Platforms

description: A pattern catalog for roving tabindex, skip links, and command palettes, evaluated against task-completion times in dense admin interfaces.
title: Keyboard-First: Navigation Patterns for Complex Web Applications

description: A controlled experiment on how loading placeholders shape perceived performance, finding that progressive disclosure beats spinners by a wide margin.
title: Skeleton Screens and the Perception of Speed
